subject: Latency spike on hosted API during autoscale pool init - Acme Apps
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeapps.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: maya.patel@acmeapps.com
Date: 2027-05-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike during scale events

Hi Karthik / Evelyn,

We started seeing big latency spikes this morning tied to spikes in traffic. When Redwood scales up additional GPU workers the first requests land with ~6-8s p95 and ~18-22s p99 — our SLAs are being missed and some user flows are timing out. This only happens when your hosted pool autoscaler adds nodes; steady-state looks fine.

We've captured traces and attached a short timeline. Can you confirm this is a cold-init / model load issue and tell us what you plan to do? This is impacting a checkout flow for several customers.

Attachments: acme-traces-0501.zip (logs), timeline.csv

Thanks,
Jordan
CTO, Acme Apps
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeapps.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-01T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike during scale events

Jordan — thanks for the report and the traces. We're investigating right away and I've looped in Evelyn (SRE) and Stephanie (Support lead). Initial hypothesis: model weights loading + kernel warmup on new GPUs is causing the tail latency during burst scale-ups. We'll run targeted traces on your pool, and I will share an interim mitigation within the hour.

Can you confirm the largest spikes were between 07:50-08:10 PT and whether you saw elevated error rates or just timeouts?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-01T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike during scale events

Quick internal notes:
- Verified p95/p99 regressions align with worker spin-up events (autoscaler events logged at 07:51, 07:56, 08:02).
- Trace artifacts show heavy disk I/O during model mmap and kernel JIT on first requests.
- No obvious application-level errors; majority are timeouts and long tails.

Immediate mitigation plan (executing):
1) Enable prefix/KV cache priming for Acme's dedicated pool (warm a small subset of nodes with representative prefixes).
2) Apply a temporary slower scale-out cadence to reduce simultaneous inits.
3) Push a prioritized runbook to customer support and start 1:1 calls if they continue to see timeouts.

Attaching a quick graphic of p95/p99 trends. Will follow up with a concrete rollback/patch plan.

Attachments: p95_p99_trends_0501.png

- Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeapps.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary mitigation applied and next steps

Jordan — quick update from our side: we've applied a temporary priming job to the Acme pool and throttled the autoscaler to stagger launches. Early telemetry for the next 30 minutes shows p95 down from ~6s to ~1.6s and p99 reduced to ~3.5s during scale events.

We also opened JIRA-INC-4521 (link below) to track the root cause and a permanent fix. Evelyn will lead a post-mortem to identify improvements to our kernel/JIT path and model mmapping.

If you can, please escalate any remaining customer-impacting requests to me directly and we'll prioritize.

Thanks for the quick report and patience.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Support, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-01T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary for VP and Eng leadership

Heads up — I'm drafting a short exec note for product and eng leadership summarizing impact and action items. Proposed one-line summary: "Acme Apps saw temporary p95/p99 tail latency increases tied to simultaneous GPU worker initialization during autoscale events; mitigations (priming + staggered scale) reduced observed tail considerably while root-cause work proceeds."

Planned next steps:
- Evelyn: RCA and perf regression test case by Friday (2027-05-07).
- Eng infra: prototype pre-warm image patch (hotfix attached) to reduce JIT/disk I/O on first request.
- Support: coordinate customer-facing timeline and possible credit offer if SLA breach invoice is likely.

Attaching the hotfix diff for review: hotfix_patch.diff

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmeapps.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: resolved for now + timeline for permanent fix

Jordan — following up with a consolidated update now that we've had a full day of monitoring.

What we did: 
- Applied targeted priming to keep a small warm set of nodes ready for burst traffic.
- Staggered autoscaler launches to avoid large concurrent model loads.
- Deployed a prototype pre-warm image that reduces first-request JIT by precomputing frequent kernels (eng working on hardening).

Outcome: measured p95 drops to ~1.2s and p99 below 3s during recent test bursts; error-rate unchanged (no application faults). We will ship the hardened pre-warm image with a tested rollout by 2027-05-10 and include a new config toggle so Acme can opt into aggressive pre-warm if they prefer lower tail latency.

Next steps for Acme:
- I will schedule a 30-min technical sync with your SREs on Wednesday 2027-05-05 to walk through the mitigation and timeline.
- Stephanie will follow up on any SLA credit discussion if you prefer that route.

Thanks again for reporting this quickly — we'll keep monitoring and let you know the moment the permanent patch ships.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook_pool_init_mitigation.pdf
